# Forward-chaining verification of: does the swallow enjoy the company of the beaver?
# Facts and rules are transcribed from the puzzle. Closed-world assumption applies
# only to facts the puzzle does not state (e.g., nobody unites with the fangtooth).

def fits(item, box):
    # Exact rectangle-in-rectangle test with 90-degree rotation allowed.
    a, b = sorted(item)
    c, d = sorted(box)
    return a <= c and b <= d

F = set()

# Given facts (only those relevant to the target chain)
F.add(("suspects_woodpecker", "elk"))           # elk suspects truthfulness of woodpecker
F.add(("teacher_assistant", "flamingo"))        # flamingo is a teacher assistant (works in education)
F.add(("dugong_unites", "flamingo"))            # dugong unites with flamingo (not fangtooth)
F.add(("tag_notebook_fits", "goat"))            # set below by exact geometry check
if not fits((18, 14), (17.8, 23.8)):
    F.discard(("tag_notebook_fits", "goat"))

# Rule1 (dachshund suspicion), Rule4 (goat brings oil tank), Rule45 (takes over emperor of bee)
# do not have their antecedents stated, so they are not derivable.

def rule_step(F):
    new = set()

    # Rule6: works in education -> does not hide cards from chihuahua
    if ("teacher_assistant", "flamingo") in F:
        new.add(("not_hide_chihuahua", "flamingo"))

    # Rule44: does not hide cards from chihuahua -> does not surrender to butterfly
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "not_hide_chihuahua":
            new.add(("not_surrender_butterfly", x))

    # Rule40: does not surrender to butterfly -> acquires photograph of snake
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "not_surrender_butterfly":
            new.add(("acquire_snake", x))

    # Rule26: acquires photograph of snake -> swears to leopard
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "acquire_snake":
            new.add(("swear_leopard", x))

    # Rule11: goat notebook fits 17.8 x 23.8 box -> goat negotiates deal with bear
    # Rule42 blocker: no animal unites with fangtooth (closed world), so it does not block.
    fangtooth_blocker = any(p == "unites_fangtooth" for (p, _) in F)
    if ("tag_notebook_fits", "goat") in F and not fangtooth_blocker:
        new.add(("negotiate_bear", "goat"))

    # Rule14: goat negotiates deal with bear -> bear calls flamingo
    if ("negotiate_bear", "goat") in F:
        new.add(("calls_flamingo", "bear"))

    # Rule36: bear calls flamingo -> flamingo dances with crab
    if ("calls_flamingo", "bear") in F:
        new.add(("dance_crab", "flamingo"))

    # Rule41: dances with crab -> does not unite with vampire
    # Rule4 (goat brings oil tank) is not derivable, so no conflict with Rule41.
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "dance_crab":
            new.add(("not_unite_vampire", x))

    # Rule17: does not unite with vampire AND swears to leopard -> suspects pigeon
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "not_unite_vampire" and ("swear_leopard", x) in F:
            new.add(("suspect_pigeon", x))

    # Rule23: some animal suspects pigeon -> swallow neglects stork
    if any(p == "suspect_pigeon" for (p, _) in F):
        new.add(("neglect_stork", "swallow"))

    # Rule30: neglects stork -> smiles at dinosaur
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "neglect_stork":
            new.add(("smile_dinosaur", x))

    # Rule29: smiles at dinosaur -> does not enjoy company of beaver
    for (p, x) in list(F):
        if p == "smile_dinosaur":
            new.add(("not_enjoy_beaver", x))

    # Rule22 / Rule3 / Rule35 etc. are not needed for the target chain.
    return new

# Fixed-point iteration
while True:
    added = rule_step(F) - F
    if not added:
        break
    F |= added

target_pos = ("enjoy_beaver", "swallow")
target_neg = ("not_enjoy_beaver", "swallow")

print("Derived not_enjoy_beaver(swallow):", target_neg in F)
print("Derived enjoy_beaver(swallow):", target_pos in F)
print("Derived flamingo dances with crab:", ("dance_crab", "flamingo") in F)
print("Derived flamingo suspects pigeon:", ("suspect_pigeon", "flamingo") in F)

# Preference check: no rule in the set concludes enjoy_beaver positively,
# so there is no conflict to resolve for the target.
if target_pos in F and target_neg in F:
    print("verdict: UNSUPPORTED (conflicting derivations)")
elif target_neg in F:
    print("verdict: disproved")
elif target_pos in F:
    print("verdict: proved")
else:
    print("verdict: unknown")

submitted = "unknown"
computed = "disproved" if target_neg in F else ("proved" if target_pos in F else "unknown")
print("submitted:", submitted, "computed:", computed)
print("CHECK PASS" if submitted == computed else "CHECK FAIL")
